html:
At the Battle of Mactan, on 27 April 1521, warriors of the chief Lapulapu killed Ferdinand Magellan on the shore of Mactan island, off Cebu, in the central Philippines.

Magellan had made an ally of the ruler of Cebu, who was baptised with his people, and tried to force Lapulapu to submit. He landed with a small force at low tide and was cut down in the shallows.

The survivors sailed on and one ship completed the first voyage around the world. Spain returned under Legazpi in 1565 and conquered the islands. Filipinos now honour Lapulapu as the first hero to resist foreign rule. See Santo Niño.
